clue.text: What 17 plays finding obstacle in course

indicators.note: the obstacle sits in the course, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a course or way to follow is a route
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a gambler plays when something blocks a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is BETTER, so the definition is the wheel game a gambler plays; 'obstacle' is the tennis or legal sense of let.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino wheel game is something a gambler (17, a better) plays.

clue.text: Player of monsters to pull old samurai's clothing

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul something heavy

indicators.note: the outermost letters of samurai wrap it like clothes, so only those edges are taken

explanation.surface: An actor dragging an old Japanese warrior's costume about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' takes the outside letters S and I of 'samurai'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bela Lugosi was the actor famed for playing Dracula and other horror monsters.

clue.text: Greek plays Brahms and Liszt trio with ease

indicators.note: rhyming slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: ease taken as written; 'with' is the join

explanation.surface: Three composers' trio played effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is Cockney rhyming slang for drunk (rhyming with 'pissed'), so it signals an anagram of TRIO plus EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus's trilogy of tragedies about Orestes is a set of Greek dramas.

clue.text: Healthy food, fare for Hollywood player

parts.note: bran is a fibre-rich health food
to fare is to do, as in 'how are you faring/doing'

explanation.surface: Wholesome diet suited to a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was a famous Hollywood actor.

clue.text: Caught god's part in Sophocles play?

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian god

explanation.surface: An actor caught playing a god in a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy the commenting group of singers is a role, a part of the play.

clue.text: Rest international player, holding six-footer back

indicators.note: the player holds the insect, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a cap is a player selected for a national side

indicators.note: the insect is read backwards

parts.note: an ant is an insect, with six legs

explanation.surface: An international sportsman resting while carrying a tall man on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect; 'back' turns ANT into TNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light sleep is a brief rest.

clue.text: Boring 13s of play a trial

parts.note: something dull and boring is dry
13 is performances; a play's run is its series of performances

explanation.surface: Dull performances of a play serving as a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or practice attempt before the real thing is a trial.

clue.text: Making slow movement in song that's playing

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: A slow passage in a song being performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or car edging forward cautiously is moving slowly, inching its way.

clue.text: Play with Italian footballers lacking freshness

parts.note: Inter Milan is an Italian football club
stale means no longer fresh

explanation.surface: A drama alongside tired Italian soccer players.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance is a drama.

clue.text: Noted work based on play, say, 12 twice

indicators.note: the round letter appears two times, one at each side, wrapping the other word

parts.note: 12 is IN THE ROUND, and a round shape is the letter O, here taken twice
to say is to tell

explanation.surface: A famous work drawn from a drama, mentioned twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is IN THE ROUND, suggesting the round letter O, which appears on both sides of TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera adapts Shakespeare's Othello: 'noted' means set to music.

clue.text: Current book in mess distorted playwright's principles

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: distorted letters are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: An up-to-date book in a mess, mangling a dramatist's ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine and dramatic method of Henrik Ibsen, Norwegian dramatist, are his principles.

clue.text: Players from station on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: station in life, social rank, is caste

explanation.surface: Actors heard from a broadcasting station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' looks like a radio station but means social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The company of actors in a production are its players.

clue.text: Hot, tense leading man — and, for Brecht, plays may be seen thus

parts.note: hot, fashionable, means in
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the leading man of a story is its hero
German for 'and', Brecht being a German playwright

explanation.surface: A sweaty, nervous lead actor in a Brecht production.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre staged with the audience surrounding the stage is presented this way.

clue.text: Playing eg Willy Loman, retiring chap's arrested by police

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Willy Loman of Death of a Salesman is a salesman, a rep

indicators.note: the chap is held by the police, sitting inside them

parts.note: the police are the force
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An actor playing Willy Loman, held by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns REP into PER; 'arrested by' puts MAN in FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting a role on stage is giving a show, a rendition of the part.

clue.text: Contest to put in crosses for these players?

indicators.note: the contest is put into the crosses, going inside them

parts.note: fords are places where a river is crossed
a war is a contest

explanation.surface: A football tactic of crossing the ball for the strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' suggests football passes but means river fords.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacking footballers who receive crosses are strikers, front players.

clue.text: Conservative government skewered by revolutionary writer in 25 play

indicators.note: the government is pierced, so the writer goes inside it

parts.note: rule is government

indicators.note: revolving the word reads it backwards

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A Tory government run through by a radical author in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the pen brand round to CIB, and 'skewered by' puts that inside the government word. 25 is MILLER, the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller (25) wrote this drama about the Salem witch trials.

clue.text: American player not in love with a shaggy-haired creature

indicators.note: not having means these letters are removed

parts.note: Al Pacino is an American actor
in taken as written
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A lovelorn American actor with a woolly animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops IN and O from ALPACINO to leave ALPAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid bred for its long woolly fleece.

clue.text: Race to enter competition with right player

indicators.note: the race enters the competition, going inside it

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in spelling bee
the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race

explanation.surface: A race entered in a competition alongside a decent player.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the odds, a gambler, is a punter.

clue.text: Way to play with voice, capturing large bird

indicators.note: the voice captures the bird, holding it inside

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
an egret is a heron-like bird

explanation.surface: Playing with a voice that catches a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking, fairly brisk, tells a performer how to play.

clue.text: In Barcelona, the regular number of players

parts.note: Spanish for 'the' is el
regular means even, steady

explanation.surface: The usual size of a team in Barcelona.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team fields this many, a side.

clue.text: Ogle diva regularly? I see plays here

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like 'see'

explanation.surface: A theatregoer eyeing the leading lady and noting where shows are put on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Vic is a historic London theatre where plays are staged.

clue.text: They're played in Hawaii and here by two card players

parts.note: here, for a British setter, is the UK
East and South are two bridge players

explanation.surface: Instruments played in Hawaii and Britain by a card-playing pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for ukuleles, small guitars associated with Hawaiian music.

clue.text: Sordid party offers something to play

parts.note: base means low, sordid
a ball is a dance party

explanation.surface: A seedy party offering something fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An American bat-and-ball sport is a game, something to play.

clue.text: Pretty daughter is not back in play

parts.note: ain't is colloquial for is not

indicators.note: the back of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pretty daughter who isn't returning to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicately small and graceful, nicely pretty.

clue.text: What Puck will make in play is what happens before PM arrives

definitions.text: What Puck will make in play
definitions.meaning: Puck promises in A Midsummer Night's Dream's epilogue to restore reparation

explanation.surface: Puck's promise contrasted with what happens before a prime minister turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' suggests the prime minister but means afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Making reparation for a wrong; Puck says 'Robin shall restore' it at the play's close.

clue.text: Playmaker, one running round Arsenal's No 7

indicators.note: the runner goes round the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a miler is a runner of the mile

indicators.note: the seventh letter of the club name is taken

explanation.surface: A football playmaker, a runner around Arsenal's number seven shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' and 'No 7' suggest football, but the definition is a writer of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Miller was a playwright, literally a maker of plays.
